title: User Persona
body:
A **persona** is a concrete description of a representative user, assembled from research. It
carries a name, a role, a goal, a level of technical confidence and the context the person is
working in.

```
Marta, 47, ward nurse
  Goal: record a patient observation and get back to the floor in under a minute
  Context: standing, gloved, interrupted constantly, shared workstation
  Technical: uses three hospital systems daily, no interest in any of them
  Frustration: being logged out between patients
```

Its function is to make the user specific. The abstract user has no constraints, adapts to
anything and is available at all times, and designing for them produces an interface that works
for the person who built it. A persona with gloved hands and forty seconds rules out a design
immediately.

Personas are built from interviews and observation, and a persona invented at a whiteboard is a
projection of the team's assumptions with a photograph attached, which is worse than none
because it lends those assumptions authority.

Two or three personas covering distinct user groups is the usual number. More than that stops
being a constraint, since a design that satisfies eight personas is designing for everybody
again.
